A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HDTree and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Despite the changed title and layout, corresponding methods and experiments can be matched reliably. Inconsistencies in reported settings are assessable differences, not missing document material.

before.justification: v1 reports original HDTree experiments, including clustering and reconstruction comparisons, lineage evaluation, component ablations, runtime measurements, and appendix sample-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results in Tables 1–5, Figures 3–5, and Appendix H. Retained results qualify even where their numerical values are unchanged.

M1.justification: The architecture and principal loss components remain. However, the stated trajectory-weighting rule changes from v1's unequal-index condition and cross-depth penalty description to penalizing auxiliary KNN edges while leaving tree edges unpenalized (v1 Eq. 9; v2 Eq. 8). This revises the specified inference objective; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image, text, and single-cell datasets, including the LineageVAE and C. elegans lineage benchmarks. Calling generation 'generative validation' introduces no demonstrated new task or input scenario. The revised ECL sample count concerns experimental settings rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding main and appendix comparisons. This includes the general-data baselines, single-cell foundation models, runtime comparators, and Waddington-OT, LineageVAE, scVI+Agg, and TreeVAE lineage comparisons. Reordered rows and revised citations do not introduce new evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Appendix D replaces depth preservation with LCA-based dendrogram purity and changes the stated LL calculation from summed log probabilities to a per-sample ELBO-based quantity. Appendices F/H revise the testing cap and describe main ECL experiments as using 838k rather than 100k cells. These substantially revise reported protocols, although retained preprocessing code still selects 100k ECL cells and reruns are not established.

E4.justification: The displayed component ablations, dimensionality study, ECL training-size sensitivity, and generation/lineage case studies are retained. v2 adds prose-only reports of robustness across KNN k values and negative correlation between ROP and tree-edit distance (Section 3.4; Appendix D), without supporting experimental details, numerical results, or plots.

E5.justification: Table 1 already specifies ten random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting in both versions. v2 Appendix D newly states that all metrics are averaged across fixed-seed runs and describes averaging FID across multiple generations. The general run count is deferred to code; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Table 5 changes tSNE+Agg runtimes from 854:10, 915:13, 1708:28, and 5879:27 to 14:14, 15:15, 28:28, and 97:59, with both tables labeled mm:ss. This reverses its speed ranking against HDTree on the first three datasets. Main accuracy tables and matched appendix score tables retain their numerical results; changed DP/ECL descriptions prevent assuming identical conditions throughout.

T1.justification: v2 revises the diffusion mathematics to include Gaussian noise in the noising expression and defines alpha-bar as a cumulative product instead of v1's 1-minus-alpha expression. Routing and edge-weight definitions are repaired, and Appendix D replaces the DP formula with intra-class LCA purity. These are targeted mathematical corrections and redefinitions, without new theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified hierarchical quantization, diffusion generation, and lineage inference. v2 adds explicit claims that tree complexity is decoupled from network size and that shared representations support sparse deep branches. It also foregrounds Waddington-landscape alignment and generation as validation of lineage plausibility, strengthening the biological framing of retained capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations, including cross-branch knowledge sharing, posterior-collapse avoidance, and interpreting binary codes as broader hierarchies. It newly acknowledges the mismatch between target-trained HDTree and zero-shot foundation models, slower diffusion sampling, and the need for biological validation. Appendix F also adds a stronger rare-population preservation claim based on the retained training-size study, which does not directly test evaluation subsampling.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository and adds metric implementation details, including Hungarian matching, empty-leaf handling, deterministic reconstruction, and diffusion likelihood/FID procedures. Loss-weight names are aligned with the method description. Hardware, software versions, principal hyperparameters, and preprocessing code are largely retained; the training pseudocode is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ghahramani et al. (2010) and Lakshminarayanan et al. (2016) to support its discussion of hierarchical representations, while dropping citations including Lan et al. (2024), He et al. (2024), and Van Den Oord et al. (2017). Positioning against branch-specific VAEs is sharpened, but the main related-work coverage remains. Consolidated TreeVAE and diffusion references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, task descriptions, method explanations, and substantial experimental discussion are rewritten. Baseline and implementation descriptions move into the appendices, the contents page and training pseudocode disappear, and limitations and an impact statement are added. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a predominantly single-column layout to a two-column conference layout, with enlarged tables, row shading, and reorganized floats. Figures 1–2 are visually restyled, and the generation and lineage figures are resized and repositioned. The existing dimensionality chart moves from v1 Table 6 to v2 Figure 5; it is not a new experiment.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical exposition, metric documentation, and qualification of baseline comparisons and sampling costs. However, it associates unchanged ECL scores with a new 838k-cell setting that conflicts with retained 100k-cell preprocessing, and introduces unsupported robustness/correlation reports. Appendix F also overextends training-size stability into evidence about test-subsampling bias. These substantive gains and new consistency problems prevent a reliable net-quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
